regs_in_letter: FD&C Act misbranding (false or misleading); no CFR section cited in letter text

cases.cat: Omission of material facts about indication
cases.claim: Beginnings of the videos introduce the use of Photofrin for the treatment of esophageal cancer (EC) and high-grade dysplasia in Barrett’s esophagus (EC video) and endobronchial non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC video), but omit specific patient populations and limitations.
cases.context: Full indications appear only at end, small plain font, ~5 seconds, alongside risk info.
cases.rationale: Failing to disclose full indications (populations and limitations) misleads about approved use.
cases.check: Rule: the first mention of each indication must include the label's population and limitation qualifiers; flag abbreviated indication statements.

cases.claim: Videos do not communicate contraindications (“PHOTOFRIN is contraindicated in patients with porphyria …”; “PDT is contraindicated in patients with tumors eroding into a major blood vessel.”) or W&P 5.1 fistula/perforation, 5.2 hemorrhage, 5.4 photosensitivity (all patients), 5.8 airway obstruction, 5.12 embryo-fetal toxicity.
cases.context: Some risk info at ~0:56 for about 10 seconds; rest only in final 5 seconds.
cases.rationale: Omitting serious contraindications and warnings creates a misleading impression of safety.
cases.check: Rule: check that every contraindication and boxed/W&P item in the label appears in the piece's risk presentation.

cases.claim: VO (2:32) (in pertinent part): “… selectively destroys the cancer cells with … a diameter of up to 1.2cm”
cases.context: PI: PDT not suitable for patients with esophageal ulcers >1 cm in diameter.
cases.rationale: Suggests patients with ulcers >1 cm can be safely treated, contradicting contraindication.
cases.check: Do any numeric eligibility/size claims conflict with contraindication thresholds in the label?

cases.cat: Lack of fair balance (risk presentation prominence)
cases.claim: “IMPORTANT WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS” presented as static, onscreen text, in small, plain font, over approximately five seconds at the end of the video, in conjunction with the indications and most common adverse reactions.
cases.context: Benefit claims in large print with colorful animated graphics; no signal that risk info follows the close of the animated portion.
cases.rationale: Risk not presented with prominence and readability reasonably comparable to benefits.
cases.check: Rule: flag video pieces where risk text is on screen for less time / smaller font than benefit text or appears only after the end of the main content.

cases.claim: “Following photodynamic therapy. Debridement may be performed if residual tumor remains” (3:34 – 3:36)
cases.context: PI describes 'mandatory debridement bronchoscopy' 2 to 3 days after light administration for endobronchial cancer.
cases.rationale: Suggests debridement is optional when label says it is mandatory.
cases.check: Does the piece describe a label-mandated procedure or monitoring step as optional?

cases.claim: VO (3:07): “Photodynamic therapy is proven to boost anti-tumor immunity and improves tumor cell immunogenicity, essentially training the body to attack the invading cancer.” | SUPER (3:14): “Systemic Neutrophilia, Acute Phase Reactants, Inflammatory Cytokines, T- Cells*”
cases.context: Supported only by a review article describing PDT generally in animal models, not Photofrin specifically.
cases.rationale: 'Proven' immune-boosting claim lacks support for Photofrin.
cases.check: Is each 'proven' mechanism claim supported by evidence specific to this product in humans rather than class-level or animal data?

cases.claim: VO (2:31): “The energy transfer generates reactive singlet oxygen which selectively destroys the cancer cells with … a diameter of up to 1.2cm.”
cases.rationale: Implies definitive, quantified NSCLC benefit not demonstrated.
cases.check: Rule: flag quantitative efficacy claims with no reference citation attached.
